page: Amazon Web Services d3en.4xlarge is a dense storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture is the defining hardware component of this configuration, supplying 111,840 GB of local HDD storage capacity. The network layer provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs included.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture oriented toward sustained aggregate throughput rather than peak single-threaded execution. Synthetic evaluations such as stress-ng and Geekbench register single-core scores in the lower quartile, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1035.0. Conversely, multi-threaded evaluations demonstrate mid-tier performance across the board, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6567.0, a PassMark CPU score of 15092.69, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 37.43 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects standard DDR4 rates, measuring 89.89 GB/sec for uncached read-only bandwidth and 47.21 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

In operational testing, the instance posted consistent midrange results, handling 13.65 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.95 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations scored 5430.88, reflecting solid transactional processing capabilities when operating in memory or against parallel spindle sets. Compute-intensive AI workloads such as 7B parameter LLM prompt processing scored in the lower quartile at 19.53 tokens per second, reinforcing that computation is not the primary strength of this hardware profile.

The primary efficiency tradeoff for the d3en.4xlarge centers on storage density versus raw latency and computation. Provisioning over 111 TB of integrated spindle disk space alongside high networking bandwidth makes this instance cost-efficient for raw capacity per node, avoiding external storage protocol overhead. However, the use of spinning disks requires sequential access patterns to maximize performance. This instance is best suited for big data file systems such as HDFS, massive log aggregation platforms, distributed data lakes, and batch analytical pipelines.
